i’m not trying to shit on self-custody. technically you can have someone professional actively worry about your self-custody setup, that’s fine too

one day, the threat level will plateau and will stop increasing exponentially on a monthly basis, and then passive security will gradually become acceptable. but today is not that day

The largest pension fund in America is tearing up the standard investing playbook.

CalPERS manages $600 billion. Its new investment chief is moving to "total portfolio" investing, which means no more fixed buckets for stocks, bonds and private assets. Every dollar competes for the best risk-adjusted return instead of filling a quota.

Translation: the most sophisticated pool of retirement money in the country no longer trusts the rigid 60/40 model most people were handed. When the team running $600 billion stops drawing hard lines between asset classes, it is worth asking why you still do.

Intellectual-property-intensive industries contribute over $7 trillion to U.S. GDP each year.

For $XFAB ER transcript:  

Just to recap, my idea on $XFAB foundry growth opportunities stemmed from SiC for 800v and photonixfab/MTP for CPO applicability.   

- $XFAB: "We are making progress in co-packaged optics".  

- "The transition to 800v... is expected to support demand for both SiC and GaN... for XFAB"  

So those analysts/people that were confidently bearposting about $XFAB that they had "0 exposure to 800V, photonics, CPO" just turned out plainly wrong. 

At the time I shared my idea, industry materials showed ASE and others cited photonixfab + XFAB as an upcoming CPO player in EU. And filings showed they had exposure names like $NVTS / $POWI in general. 

So glad $XFAB went out to explicitly clear things up to state they were developing in CPO/800v.   

Okay back to the ER:  

- "We continue to expect photonics volume production to start in 2028".  Company currently has three silicon photonics projects in development with key partners.   

I thought it would ramp sometime in H2 2027, but was probably early by a few months. 

- Several new data center design wins, eg. 3 new SiC design wins (consistent with general 2027 ramp as 800v deployment takes off).  

So once those ramp in 2027-2028, (markets tend to price things ahead of time), I'd expect $XFAB to be rerated based on growth opportunities.   

TLDR:  
- Current revenue numbers not as impressive.
- $XFAB confirmed direct exposure to CPO and 800V shifts (biggest win for thesis) 
- 800V exposure opportunities for SiC (should be 2027)
-  Timeline is 2028 ramp for photonics volume production  

Happy exposure thesis to CPO/800V was confirmed from this ER. Might be a bit of waiting for revenue ramp.

You're going to get 35% pullbacks. You'll get 50% drawdowns.

None of it matters if you understand what you own.

Because this is a long game. I think these networks become the pension for an entire generation. You don't trade your way there. You build a thesis, you accumulate, you keep something back for the big sell-offs, and you let time and adoption do the work.

The volatility is the price of admission. The people who make it are the ones who stop flinching at it.

Seeing a lot of callbacks to Zach's post about iPhones vs hardware wallets.

I want to make something clear: Zach's point about UX is valid but if you can reason about a hardware wallet, IT IS STILL THE BEST OPTION.

The cold card attack was due to bad entropy in their seed-generation path. Many wallets have very very good entropy. Ledger specifically is tested/certified against AIS-31.

iPhones have good entropy too! But software-wallet key generation adds a trust requirement in the app, dependencies, OS/runtime, and device state. A bug in any of those can turn into compromised wallets. It also means handling signing keys inside a general-purpose, (potentially) internet-connected device.

A hardware wallet’s main advantage is that it isolates key generation and signing in a dedicated device, while letting you verify important transaction details on a trusted display. That materially reduces the attack surface.

Hardware wallets aren’t perfect. Neither are software wallets. But for users who can manage the UX safely, dedicated hardware remains the best option.

Basically the r/r for holding STRC at $100 is atrocious if we know they will always hit the ATM at $100, because you get all the downside volatility and only 1% yield every month as upside. Given the type of volatility STRC has (10% swings), if you short it at $100, you're almost certain that you'll get out in profit on its next drawdown.

Strategy claims that they target a 1% range at $99-$100, but that's physically impossible, because even if the dividend rate is variable in theory, in the short-term the div rate is fixed, meaning it will have a similar volatility profile as STRF, ie at least 10% swings.
If you cap the upside at $100, the 10% swings will be capped at $100 and you mechanically decrease the bottom of these volatile moves. I think it's much more realistic to target a $95-$105 range, because the average price of STRC would then be around $100 (which is the goal). In the current situation, by trying to be cute and "guarantee that STRC won't top $100", Strategy forces the whole thing to trade in a $90-$100 range (at best), meaning the average price of STRC is significantly below $100.
